stories.title: Man charged with murder after stabbing at IPAS centre
stories.summary: A 49-year-old man has been charged in connection with an incident in which a man died, and another was injured following a stabbing at an International Protection Accommodation Services centre in Co Kerry. Emergency services were called to the scene at Ballymullen Barracks in Tralee yesterday shortly after 5.20am. Ismail Mustaph Hussan was brought before a special sitting of Killarney District Court this evening. He is charged with the murder of Muhudin Osman Suleyman at Ballymullen Barracks yesterday morning contrary to common law. The Somali national is further charged with Section 3 assault causing harm to another man at the same location. Detective Sergeant James Hurley of Tralee Garda Station gave evidence of arrest, charge and caution.

stories.title: EY Ireland's annual revenue grows by 4.4% to €880m
stories.summary: Professional services firm EY Ireland has reported continued growth for its financial year to the end of June 2026. EY Ireland reported annual revenues of €880m on the island of Ireland, an increase of 4.4% on the €843m reported in the previous year. Revenue in the Republic of Ireland reached €810m, an increase of 3.7% on last year's revenue of €781m, it added. The company's headcount across the island stood at more than 5,600 at the end of June 2026, with almost 100 different nationalities working across all areas of the business. It now has 158 Equity Partners across the island of Ireland, including 144 in the Republic of Ireland. During the year, Taoiseach Micheál Martin officially opened its new headquarters at Wilton Park in Dublin, as well as its expanded Cork offices on Lapps Quay.

stories.title: Restored nature hits record level, still off target - UN
stories.summary: Countries are restoring about 252 million hectares of nature, a record level according to a United Nations report, but this still falls short of global 2030 targets. "This report captures the largest documented restoration effort in history," said Doreen Robinson at the UN Environment Programme. The restored area is equivalent to the size of Argentina or Algeria. But the report estimates the pace of restoration efforts must "triple" to meet the 2030 target of one billion, and funding will need to increase sharply, particularly from the private sector. Nature restoration efforts recorded in 149 countries have mostly taken place on land, with 232 million hectares involved, compared with 11 million hectares of inland waters and 5.7 million hectares of marine and coastal waters. This "lags far behind ambition in both freshwater (inland water) and marine and coastal ecosystems, yet these ecosystems are degrading at the highest rates," the report warned.

stories.title: Arteta has the band back together after Fleetwood whack
stories.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says his side's first Premier League victory at Liverpool in 14 years was inspired by their shock Carabao Cup exit at Fleetwood. The Gunners suffered a humiliating penalty shoot-out defeat to the League Two side on Tuesday. But the champions responded in style on Sunday, claiming a hard-fought 1-0 win at Anfield to move top of the Premier League table. Arteta said: "It has been such a long time without having this winning feeling here. "We are extremely proud of the team and the players and what everyone has done, especially in the conditions in which we arrived to this game – the defeat against Fleetwood looks the end of the world, but then you have to pick yourself up. "How the hell can you go out of the cup when you shoot 27 times and have the chances we had against a team who had one shot on target? Then you look so silly but I had the feeling now was the moment.

stories.title: Untangling the Hallowe'en story - we didn't really invent it
stories.summary: Folklorist Michael Fortune takes a deep dive into the myths and legends behind Hallowe'en... I’ve been recording and sharing content about Hallowe’en from around the country and beyond for the past 20+ years and although I spent many of these years promoting the Irish connection to Hallowe’en, I now see a lot dubious claims circulating that we invented it and it was just an Irish tradition. We certainly influenced the American tradition, but we didn’t really invent it. Most of our Hallowe’en experiences are shared with our neighbours over in Scotland, the Isle of Man, Wales and parts of England, as well as our mainland European neighbours which is tied in with their St. Martin’s Eve traditions on the 11th of November or 'Old Hallowe’en’ as it was called by some. I do not have the word count to unravel the complete Hallowe’en tangle, but I will spell out the four main distinctive elements which make up the Irish Hallowe’en experience; Food/Harvest, Mumming/Disguise, The Dead/Light and Tricks/Devilment. I will share just one with you - the Mumming/Disguise element. Unlike other parts of the county and country, the Hallowe'en tradition along the north east coast of Wexford where I grew up was very strong. Many of us grew up knowing Hallowe’en as ‘All Hollow's Eve’, ‘All Holland’ or ‘Vizzarding Night’, while in other parts of north Wexford it was known as ‘Blackmen Night’ or ‘Collicking Night’. In other parts of the country they called it Púca Night, Pookie Night, Juggy Night, Snap Apple Night and over in Newfoundland, Colcannon Night.

stories.title: Ash shirt collaboration attracts fans around the world
stories.summary: Fans of the band Ash from across the world have sold out a Northern Ireland football team's special collaboration shirt with the threesome. The Ash x Ards FC collab marks the 30th anniversary of the group’s debut album 1977, recreating the original album cover in black, green and white. Lead singer Tim Wheeler also suggested the number 77 be put on the back of the shirt for which a third run is currently being planned to cope with demand from Taiwan, Japan and Australia as well as the United States. Although the band originally hails from Downpatrick, drummer Rick McMurray attended Ards FC matches in his youth with his father. The collab was announced with a video on social media last Monday featuring McMurray and Wheeler, along with Mark Hamilton wearing the shirts. McMurray says from the age of three his father took him to see Ards FC play every weekend, adding: "Now look at us, we have Ards FC football shirts, 1977 based, ain’t they pretty?".

He's a firm fitness fan, and does triathlons, surfing, kite surfing and has represented Ireland in University Rugby as a medical student. He is a Consultant Colorectal and General Surgeon working in CUH.

President Connolly said Ms Mageean stood out not just for her "exceptional talent", but for her "strength and perseverance, for her clear speaking, and for her determination to succeed".

stories.title: Mulcahy: We're representing Cork - we're disappointed
stories.summary: Glen Rovers manager Tomás Mulcahy admitted his side couldn't live with Clare champions Inagh-Kilnamona as they exited the Munster club championship at the first hurdle. Mulcahy guided the Blackpool side their first Cork Premier Senior Hurling championship in 10 years a fortnight ago but they were always second best against the first-time champions from Clare, going 0-06 to 0-01 behind after 10 minutes, a gap they were never really able to peg back. It's 2009 since the Cork senior champions last added the Munster crown to the Sean Óg Murphy Cup, when the great Newtownshandrum side of the 2000s won their third provincial crown of the decade. Sarsfields did become the first Cork side to win the Munster club SHC in 15 years in 2024 and reached the subsequent All-Ireland final where they lost to Na Fianna. However, the Glanmire club were not Cork champions at the time, having lost that season's county final to East Cork divisional outfit Imokilly. Glen Rovers won the inaugural Munster club championship back in 1964 - prior to the establishment of the All-Ireland series - and two further titles in 1973 and 1977. However, their three recent tilts have been underwhelming. "But you've got to give credit to Inagh-Kilnamona. They came with a gameplan. They dropped a bit deep. They had a man in front of [Eoin] O'Leary. They saw the threat he was in the Cork championship. So it took us a while to adapt to that

stories.title: Klum transforms into bloodied hand for Halloween bash
stories.summary: Heidi Klum underwent a bloody transformation to become a giant, gruesome severed hand for her annual Halloween party in New York on Saturday. German-American model Klum, famed for her extravagant Halloween costumes, looked unrecognisable as she transformed into a severed human hand. The star shared several photos posed up as the bloodied limb, accompanied by a series of hand-based puns, ahead of the party, 25 years after she began hosting the event. Zendaya, Cara Delevingne, Kourtney Kardashian, Neil Patrick Harris and his husband David Burtka were among other celebrities getting in the Halloween spirit over the weekend. Harris and Burtka were dressed as the twins from The Shining. Actress Zendaya wowed as she dressed as Halle Berry, recreating the star's look from the New York premiere of X-Men in 2000.

She underwent a second surgery on her achilles in 2024 after withdrawing from the Olympics and was diagnosed with cancer in 2025. Her deep roots in her beloved town of Portaferry on the tip of Ards Peninsula forged an early love with a different sport though. Mageean's sporting talent first shone through on the pitches of Portaferry GAC with a hurl in her hand playing camogie alongside her sisters Máire and Nuala. stories.title: Defensive masterclass at Anfield sends Arsenal back top
stories.summary: Arsenal recorded a first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years but needed some help from Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker, whose first-half error led to Kai Havertz's solitary goal in the 1-0 win. Not since manager Mikel Arteta was running the Gunners’ midfield in 2012 had they tasted victory in the red half of Merseyside and they were tested to the limit in ending that run. However, if it is one thing Arteta’s side are well-drilled at it is seeing out games having maximised their opportunities and the celebrations in front of the visiting fans having moved top of the table showed how significant they felt this result was. And while most of the football was played by Liverpool after going behind it did not bring any rewards – partly due to poor judgement and execution but also bad luck. How Jurrien Timber’s tug on the shirt of Alexander Isak as he tried to connect with a header escaped the eagle eye of VAR will remain a question, especially as they were quick to look into a more regular coming together of Cody Gakpo and Christos Tzolis. By then the hosts were already behind after another miscalculation by Alisson.

stories.title: Behind the music - David Eamon
stories.summary: Wexford soul artist David Eamon has released his debut single, Beautiful Thoughts. We asked him the BIG questions . . . A student at Dublin music college BIMM, he recently played Whelan's Ones to Watch festival, and has also supported Irish acts Esmeralda Road, Child of Prague, Syano, Dog Swim and Mount Pyrus; as well as international acts Xavier Omär (US) and MT Jones (UK). I studied Law for two and a half years before I left to pursue music. Then, I worked as a singing waiter in a Teppanyaki Restaurant. Which is part of why I love cooking (signature dish is Chicken Ramen). Yearning, but make it groovy. I write most of the songs with the guitar and then my wonderful band help me bring to life what I hear playing along in my head, but they make it so much better. Like most songwriters, I try to either create, re-create or amalgamate the songs I love and want to listen to more of. And I try to make both myself; and whoever hears them feel something in the process, either with your heart, your head or your feet. Ideally, all three at the same time.

stories.title: Longest truce of Ukraine war ends in Kherson
stories.summary: The longest truce of the Ukraine war, limited to the eastern Kherson region, has ended after Russia refused the offer of an extension, Ukrainian officials said. The rare pause in fighting, which began early Tuesday, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and came as the Ukraine war grinds through its fifth year. Neither side reported violations after the truce began, in what one Ukrainian lawmaker described as the "biggest de-escalation since 2022". "The ceasefire, which was in effect from 27 October to 1 November has ended," said Ukraine's Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets. He called the temporary truce "an important step in our joint humanitarian efforts" with Russia. US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume this month, having been effectively frozen since the United States and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February.

stories.title: Euro round-up: Real win fourth straight; Juve down Napoli
stories.summary: Real Madrid scored three first-half goals as they picked up a fourth successive La Liga victory, beating Racing Santander 3-0. Jose Mourinho's side backed up last week’s El Clasico win with a perfect first half showing after Kylian Mbappe struck from the penalty spot and Jude Bellingham’s fourth goal of the season. The pick of the goals came from summer signing Yan Diomande, who scored a third goal in four matches when the ball dropped to him and he fired into the top left corner. Real Sociedad’s four-match winning run came to an end after they lost 2-1 to Athletic Bilbao thanks to first-half goals from Inaki Williams and Alex Berenguer (penalty). Lazio’s brilliant start to the Serie A season continued as they extended their lead at the top to three points with a 2-1 win over Cagliari. The Sardinians hit the front through M’Bala Nzola but Lazio came from behind to get a ninth win from their first 10 games thanks to goals from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti.

stories.title: Harry Styles dresses as 'pizza rat' for final NY show
stories.summary: Harry Styles wore a giant rat costume as he celebrated Halloween on the final night of his Madison Square Garden residency. The singer, 32, held a large foam pizza slice as he strutted on stage on Saturday, wearing the brown furry costume, which featured pink feet and a long tail, topped with a pair of sunglasses. Styles appeared to be referencing a viral video of a rat carrying a pizza slice down the steps of a New York City subway station. The Grammy-winning singer was joined on stage by members of his band, who continued the theme by dressing up as New York City landmarks and references. Later in the night, Styles took off the rat costume but kept his fluffy ears and tail, instead opting for a pair of brown shorts and a white T-shirt which said: "I am a rat." In videos from the show, Styles’ partner Zoe Kravitz was spotted in the stands dancing and singing along, wearing a plastic bag as a mini dress featuring the words "thank you, have a nice day".

stories.title: US judge dismisses Trump lawsuit over Epstein letter
stories.summary: A US judge has dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation case against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that he sent a birthday letter to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Mr Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the president's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman. Mr Murdoch is the founder of News Corp. which owns the Wall Street Journal. The report piled scrutiny on Mr Trump from both Democrats and his own Republican party, who rejected the president's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein. In the ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed Mr Trump's lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Mr Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Judge Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April. The judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Mr Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice".

stories.title: NFL: Detroit end Minnesota Vikings' unbeaten start
stories.summary: The Detroit Lions picked up a third successive victory with a closely fought 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings who lost for the first time this season. The Vikings led 7-6 at the break thanks to Justin Jefferson's touchdown but the Lions turned things around in the second half. Jahmyr Gibbs gave the Lions a lead in the third quarter before TJ Hockenson's fourth-quarter effort put the Vikings' noses back in front, but the decisive touchdown came when Jared Goff found Jameson Williams to grab the win. The Buffalo Bills earned a sixth win of the campaign with a 36-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens as Josh Allen and James Cook ran for touchdowns and Allen threw two more to DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid. The Jacksonville Jaguars ran riot with six touchdowns as they earned a crushing 42-7 win over the beleaguered Indianapolis Colts, who suffered their sixth defeat of the season. The Colts have already sacked general manager Chris Ballard and traded away star players DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson, with more expected to follow. The Las Vegas Raiders produced a fightback as they came from nine points down at the break to win 38-33 against the New York Jets thanks to Dylan Laube's kick-return touchdown, Brock Bowers' second score of the game, a rare rushing touchdown for quarterback Kirk Cousins and Jalen Nailor's catch.

The Cusher Road has since reopened to traffic and the PSNI has appealed for witnesses to contact them.

stories.title: WSL round-up: Hayes header turns Palace tie for Brighton
stories.summary: Caitlin Hayes was on the scoresheet as Brighton came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 2-1 at Broadfield Stadium. Anabel Blanchard put the visitors ahead 34 minutes into the tie but Ireland international Hayes struck with a trademark header just before the hour mark to level the game before Sophie Peskett notched the winner five minutes later. The defeat made it three losses on the bounce for Palace and leaves them second from the bottom. Hayes' Brighton are up to sixth on the back of three wins in four games. Chelsea moved to the top of the Women's Super League table with an emphatic 6-0 victory over strugglers Charlton at The Valley. Katie McCabe set up the opening goal after just three minutes for Nathalie Bjorn as the Blues blew Charlton away with four goals in 19 minutes to kill the contest early. After Bjorn’s opener on her first start of the season, Melvine Malard bagged either side of Ellie Carpenter’s effort.

stories.summary: A Dublin city councillor has criticised anti-social behaviour in Cherry Orchard last night and said people involved "terrorised the community". There were multiple incidents reported in the area during Halloween night, with footage circulating online showing cars being driven dangerously, colliding with other vehicles and fireworks being set off in front of crowds. Cars were also set alight, while a number of other fires were also started. Sinn Féin councillor for Ballyfermot-Drimnagh Daithí Doolan described the events as "traumatising" for those living in the area. "The people living there are hard-working families who want the best for their children and for the wider community," he said. Cllr Doolan said a "small minority of people decided to get cars, rob them, burn them out, and terrorise the community".

stories.title: Con O'Callaghan two-pointer sends Cuala to quarter-finals
stories.summary: Con O'Callaghan rode to Cuala's rescue with a dramatic late two-pointer to help propel the Dublin champions through to an AIB Leinster club SFC quarter-final tie. A ding-dong Parnell Park encounter hung in the balance at the end of the hour mark, when O'Callaghan took on the responsibility and drilled an orange flag score to put his team two points clear. That's how it stayed with a Harry Plunkett inspired Tullamore unable to claw back the points they needed in the two minutes of stoppage time. It was a cruel loss on four-in-a-row Offaly champions Tullamore who were beaten narrowly by the same Dalkey opposition two years ago. Cuala found themselves in a tricky position this time, trailing by four points with just over 20 minutes to go. But the big game experience of Derek Dunne's crew came to the fore from there on with Cuala outscoring Tullamore by 0-08 to 0-01 in a crucial period between the 39th and 54th minutes. David O'Dowd and Niall O'Callaghan capped fine games with important scores for Cuala during that surge. It still came right down to the wire as Tullamore refused to go down without a fight and King Con once again proved the difference with that two-pointer winner.

stories.title: Israel's election revealed a divided country
stories.summary: To report on last week's general election in Israel was to report on two different countries. There is the Israel seen from abroad - a country increasingly isolated over its war in Gaza and its conduct in the Occupied West Bank, the one facing accusations of genocide, sanctions and boycotts. And then there is the Israel I found on the ground - where that global isolation, and the war that caused it, barely featured in the election campaign. In some ways, it's actually not surprising. Three years later, the attacks on 7 October 2023, the deadliest day in the country's history, remain the lens through which almost everything there is seen. In a nation very much built in the shadow of the Holocaust, those attacks revived the oldest of Jewish fears - that they could never be fully safe, not even in a state of their own. Many in Ireland, where sympathy for the Palestinians runs deep, would argue that those attacks did not happen in a vacuum - but came after decades of brutal occupation, and that Israel’s response has amounted to the collective punishment of more than two million people.

stories.title: Galway's Nolan secures DP World Tour card in Mallorca
stories.summary: Liam Nolan has secured his DP World Tour card for 2027 with an excellent final round of 67 at the Hotel Planner Tour's Grand Final in Mallorca, Spain. Nolan entered today's final round sitting 12th on the 'Road to Mallorca' with the top 15 at the end of this week guaranteed a main Tour card for next year. The Galwayman proceeded to produce his lowest round of the week with his five-under-par 67 made up of seven birdies and just two dropped shots to leave him on 11-under-par overall, 11 off the winning total of -22 posted by France's Julien Sale. All of that means Nolan ended his campaign in tenth position on the Road to Mallorca and will play on the DP World Tour in the New Year. "It's nice to be done. To have the card is pretty surreal," Nolan told the HotelPlanner 'X' account. "Even after the win [in Abu Dhabi] you still have to work so hard to get a card but now the work is done. So, I can just relax for about a week and then get back to work!"

stories.title: Rise in non-Irish citizens in homeless accommodation
stories.summary: The number of non-Irish citizens in emergency accommodation has significantly increased, the Minister for Housing has said. James Browne said that nationally around 50% of those in emergency accommodation are non-Irish citizens, and in Dublin that figure is 58% and rising. "But it's challenging because homelessness is really rising in Dublin, where there is an acute housing shortage, not just social houses." "Nobody is saying because they're non-citizens they shouldn't be housed, but we have to understand where people are coming from into emergency accommodation, and what their needs are to get them back out in terms of how you address it. "So, it's understanding the facts is absolutely critical to addressing it, and kind of blinding ourselves away from what the facts is not going to help address the situation," he said. Mr Browne said they have to "deal with the facts" and "we have to understand where people are coming from into emergency accommodation and what their needs are to get them back out".

stories.title: October worst on record for overcrowding, says INMO
stories.summary: October was the worst on record for hospital overcrowding, with 12,672 patients treated in corridors, on chairs or trolleys, according to the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation. In a statement, the INMO said overcrowding is consistently worse than previous years, and that so far this year 111,000 patients have been treated on trolleys in acute hospitals around the country. INMO general secretary Phil Ní Sheaghdha said that patients who are being treated on trolleys or chairs "can expect a worse health outcome than those who are lucky enough to be treated on a bed." She added: "This is a complete crisis, with higher numbers of patients than ever being completely let down by the health service. But rather than take steps to improve this situation, the Government and the HSE are implementing measures that are guaranteed to make it worse." Ms Ní Sheaghdha called for a reversal of the recruitment freeze implemented by the Department of Health. She said a continued lack of targeted investment in the health service "is going to lead to the services and staff being run into the ground."

stories.title: FBI says North Korea behind $6bn crypto theft
stories.summary: Binance said it had resumed withdrawals after more than $6 billion in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack the FBI said North Korea was responsible for. The US law enforcement agency's statement came as Binance offered reassurances it was covering the losses from the hacking attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90% of what was stolen. Binance is the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the cyberattack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. The FBI confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5bn theft from the Bybit platform in February last year. "The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026," the statement said.

stories.summary: President Donald Trump said that the United States has knocked out much of Iran's military but still has to "take care of" one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked. "You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. The Iranian government denied any nuclear work is carried out there.

stories.summary: The Trump administration has pressed a criminal investigation in to Alaska's pivotal US Senate race and said it would likely take its fight over thousands of California postal ballots to ⁠the Supreme Court, as the midterm campaign for control of Congress entered its final weekend. The closely contested race is seen as crucial to Democrats’ hopes of taking the Senate in Tuesday’s vote.
